title: BindableFunction
summary: Same-side request/response: Invoke() calls another script's OnInvoke and returns its result — like RemoteFunction without the network. Rarely needed; direct function calls usually win.

methods.name: Invoke
methods.description: Calls the OnInvoke handler assigned on this side and returns its result.

properties.name: OnInvoke
properties.description: Assigned handler: `bindable.OnInvoke = function(...) return value end`. Must be set before Invoke is called.

details.heading: Same serialization caveat as BindableEvent
details.body: Arguments and return values pass by deep copy; metatables are stripped.

explanation.whatItIs: A function call routed through an Instance so another script can implement it. 'Whoever owns this, answer me.'
explanation.whyItExists: Historically: plugins and loosely-coupled systems that couldn't hold direct references to each other.
whenToUse: Occasionally in plugin architectures or editor tooling
When scripts truly can't share module references and you need a reply
whenNotToUse: Almost always prefer requiring a module and calling its function directly — simpler, typed, faster, no copy semantics
Never for client/server — it doesn't cross the boundary
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Script A:  local result = bindable:Invoke(10)
Script B:  bindable.OnInvoke = function(x) return x * 2 end
           -- result is 20
```
tips: If you reach for BindableFunction, ask first: 'can this be a ModuleScript function?' — usually yes
commonMistakes: Invoking before OnInvoke is assigned — errors
Expecting tables to pass by reference — they're copied

examples.title: Minimal usage
examples.code:
-- Provider Script:
local bindable = script.Parent.SomeBindableFunction
bindable.OnInvoke = function(a, b)
    return a + b
end

-- Consumer Script:
local bindable = game.ServerScriptService.SomeBindableFunction
print(bindable:Invoke(20, 22))   --> 42
